raw_response:
Well, let me think through this year like I do every year, sitting at the kitchen table before spring work starts.

I'm getting on in years — 74 this year, been working this land since I was a boy. My back isn't what it was. My son works in town at the factory, sends money home but can only come back to help during cotton picking in autumn. My wife still helps in the field but she's slower now too. So labor — that's the thing I think about first, more than money even.

Six mu isn't much. The way I do it: four mu in cotton on the western plot (that's the sandy ground, cotton likes it there, and it's been cotton for years so I know what it does), and two mu in the back plot for wheat-maize so we have our own flour and corn for the chickens. Can't count on buying everything from the market — prices go up, and my pension is small.

**Cotton (4 mu):** I'll plant around April 20th, when the soil warms up. I use the same variety I bought from the seed shop last year — it did okay, about 250 jin of lint per mu. Seed costs around 50 yuan per mu. Before planting I'll put down compound fertilizer, maybe 40 jin per mu (that's about 20 kg), which gives roughly 10-12 kg of N and some P and K together. The extension guy two years ago told me I should split the nitrogen and topdress at flowering, and I do put a little urea on at budding time, maybe 10 kg of urea per mu. That's enough — more and the cotton grows too much leaf and the bolls don't set well, I learned that the hard way back in the 90s. Irrigation twice usually — once after sowing if it's dry, once at flowering. Well water costs money to pump but if the bolls don't get water at flowering you lose half your crop. Pesticide I have to spray — bollworm every year, maybe 3-4 sprays through summer. Weeds I pull by hand when I can, use a bit of herbicide on the rows.

**Wheat (2 mu):** Already in the ground since last October. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, around 30 jin per mu. Now in spring I'll topdress urea, about 15 kg per mu at jointing when it greens up. Irrigate at jointing and again at grain-filling — two times usually, three if spring is very dry. Should get 400 kg per mu, same as last year. Wheat harvest early June.

**Maize (2 mu):** Right after wheat comes off — no time to waste, tight turnaround, just a week. I use no-till, drill the seed right into the stubble. Saves time and my back. Seed is hybrid, about 40 yuan per mu. One bag of compound fertilizer at planting per mu (about 40 jin), then if the maize looks yellow at knee-high I'll topdress another 10 kg of urea. One irrigation in August if it's dry, sometimes no irrigation needed if the rains come. Should get 450 kg per mu.

Total input spending — I try to keep it under 2,500 yuan for the whole farm. Any more and there's nothing left if something goes wrong.
